questions.prompt: Why is SYSVOL readable by every authenticated user in the domain?
options: It is a misconfiguration that should be corrected
By design -- every machine must be able to fetch its own policy files, so anything an administrator stores there is domain-wide readable
Only domain controllers can actually read it
Because Group Policy requires anonymous access
questions.explanation: SYSVOL must be world-readable for Group Policy to function at all. The security consequence is that any secret placed there is readable by any domain account.

questions.prompt: What does write access to a GPO linked to an OU give an attacker?
options: Read access to that OU's user list only
Code execution on every machine in that OU, via mechanisms like an Immediate Scheduled Task or startup script
The ability to rename the OU
questions.explanation: Group Policy is a domain-wide code distribution mechanism. Write access to a linked GPO converts directly into code execution across every machine the GPO applies to.

questions.prompt: Why does MS14-025 not fully resolve the GPP cpassword exposure?
options: Because the patch was never released
Because it prevented creating new cpassword entries but did not retroactively remove existing files already sitting in SYSVOL
Because the encryption key was never actually published
Because it only applies to Windows workstations
questions.explanation: The update stopped new GPP password entries from being created, but legacy Groups.xml and similar files with cpassword values persist in many long-lived domains, still readable by any authenticated user.

questions.prompt: Why is comparing GPT.INI's version number against the directory object's versionNumber useful?
options: It reveals the GPO's creation date
A mismatch indicates one half of the GPO changed without the other, which is not how legitimate edits behave
It shows which users have read the GPO
It is required for replication to function
questions.explanation: A GPO exists as both a directory object and a SYSVOL folder. Legitimate changes update both in step, so a version mismatch between the two halves points at direct manipulation.
